sonnet.problem: The right answer 'Their own appetites' is a different kind of thing from the two wrong answers, 'The rulers of Rome' and 'The teachers of the law', which are groups of people. It stands out as the odd one, and the question asks 'Who' while the right answer is not a who.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

sonnet.problem: The two right words, 'good' and 'evil', can swap places and still make a grammatical sentence ('wise about what is evil and innocent about what is good'). Neither fits only its own blank. The baker also has to recall wording from a verse no card has told.
sonnet.rule: With two blanks, each right word fits only its own blank. If the two right words could swap places, use one blank or another question type.

sonnet.problem: The story card says of God and Satan, 'it is NOT a fair fight'. That signals who wins and gives away the answer to the next card, a true or false question on whether the God of peace will crush Satan. It also puts a joke on God's side of the moment instead of the human side.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
